attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Projection carriers cannot simultaneously keep the lower bound weak in the semantic source size and transfer it to exclusion of all polynomial SAT exponents.
steps: Generalize the padded SAT carrier to a projection family H_N with embedded SAT length ell(N) and linear validity/decoder overhead.
Assume the target negation: SAT has nonuniform circuits of size m^c for a fixed exponent c at every length m.
Compose the SAT_{ell(N)} circuit with pi_N and V_N, obtaining SIZE(H_N)<=O(N log N)+ell(N)^c.
Combine with the source lower bound SIZE(H_N)>K N^{1+epsilon} on infinitely many N.
If ell(N)=N^{alpha+o(1)}, contradiction is forced only for c<(1+epsilon)/alpha.
To rule out all fixed c, require ell(N)=N^{o(1)} on the lower-bound support.
But then the source threshold N^{1+epsilon} equals ell(N)^{omega(1)}, so the lower bound is no longer barely nontrivial relative to the embedded SAT instance size.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument is a valid route-failure certificate for a controlled interface. It proves neither the source lower bound nor P != NP, and it does not address nonprojection carriers such as MCSP or proof-complexity encodings.

assumptions: epsilon>0 and K>0 are fixed constants.
The source lower-bound model is nonuniform Boolean circuit SIZE on the explicit family H_N.
The decoder pi_N has output length exactly ell(N) after harmless SAT padding.
The validity and projection circuitry have size O(N log N), or more generally o(N^{1+epsilon}).
The claimed source lower bound SIZE(H_N)>K N^{1+epsilon} holds for infinitely many N in the support.
definitions: source object: H_N is a total N-bit Boolean carrier H_N(y)=V_N(y) AND SAT_m(pi_N(y)) with m=ell(N), shorter formulas padded to length m, and lower bounds measured against fan-in two nonuniform circuits.
target object: SAT_m against nonuniform polynomial-size circuits; the target consequence SAT notin P/poly is obtained only if every fixed exponent c is excluded.
controlled interface: a linear-size validity/decoder circuit and one SAT_m circuit compose to compute H_N with no per-instance advice or hidden nonuniform table beyond the target SAT circuit.

target-preserving condition: lower-bound lengths N form an infinite support, m=ell(N) is unbounded and known, interface overhead is o(N^{1+epsilon}), and the projection is fixed uniformly enough for composition to preserve the target circuit assumption.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: take ell(N)=N^{1/2} and epsilon=0.1; SAT circuits of size n^3 induce H_N circuits of size N^{1.5+o(1)}, so an N^{1.1} lower bound for H_N is compatible with SAT in SIZE(n^3).

candidate_lemmas.statement: For any linear-overhead projection-padding carrier H_N that computes SAT on an embedded formula length m=ell(N), an i.o. lower bound SIZE(H_N)>K N^{1+epsilon} transfers only to SAT exponent c satisfying ell(N)^c=o(N^{1+epsilon}). Thus ell(N)=N^{alpha+o(1)} excludes only c<(1+epsilon)/alpha, while ell(N)=N^{o(1)} can exclude all fixed c but makes the source threshold superpolynomial in the embedded SAT length. This is a valid route-level no-go for projection carriers, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: The bridge uses a black-box composition upper bound SIZE(H_N)<=T(N)+G(SIZE(F_{m(N)})).
Constants hidden in T(N) are independent of the target exponent c.
The lower-bound assertion is asymptotic on an infinite set of N.
definitions: source model: arbitrary carrier H_N with a compositional upper bound from target circuits plus interface overhead T(N).
target model: any nonuniform target family F_m whose assumed small circuits are composed through the interface.
threshold: source lower bound K N^{1+epsilon} against the same circuit basis as the composed upper bound.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: a verifier of size N^{1.2} cannot magnify an N^{1.1} lower bound, even if the target circuit part is tiny.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents false promotion of bridges whose checker or decoder already exceeds the claimed barely-nontrivial threshold.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Any bridge with interface overhead T(N)=N^{1+delta+o(1)} can use an N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound only when delta<epsilon; otherwise the overhead floor alone prevents contradiction with the target upper bound.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a named nonprojection carrier, such as MCSP or a proof-complexity object, gives a quantified barely-nontrivial lower bound whose transfer excludes an unbounded target exponent range without nonuniform leakage.

dependency_updates.description: For projection-padding carriers, magnification is exactly the exponent inequality ell(N)^c=o(N^{1+epsilon}); no theorem in this interface yields a weak-source route to SAT notin P/poly.
The source lower bound must be judged against both the external length N and the embedded SAT length ell(N); subpolynomial ell(N) makes N^{1+epsilon} semantically strong.
SAT notin P/poly requires exclusion of every fixed exponent c, not merely the finite window c<(1+epsilon)/alpha.

The active obstruction here is quantitative and relativizing. Natural-proofs and algebrization folklore are not needed; a future source proof must still avoid any large constructive property if it targets pseudorandom-function-strength circuit lower bounds.

falsifiers: falsifier: ell(N)=N^{1/2}, epsilon=0.1, and target exponent c=3 leave the composed H_N upper bound above N^{1.1}, so the bridge cannot refute SAT in SIZE(n^3).
falsifier: interface overhead N^{1+delta} with delta>=epsilon masks any target-circuit saving and collapses the quantitative transfer.
falsifier: a decoder using N-bit nonuniform advice can make H_N hard for reasons unrelated to SAT, causing nonuniform leakage and invalid target preservation.
falsifier: proving H_N>N^{1+epsilon} only at lengths where the projection image is empty or bounded gives no target-class consequence.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 5 converts the padding quarantine into a general projection-carrier dichotomy. The valid bridge says N^{1+epsilon} lower bounds transfer through ell(N) only when ell(N)^c is below the threshold. Positive polynomial embedding length gives only a bounded exponent window; subpolynomial embedding length gives all exponents but turns the source lower bound into ell(N)^{omega(1)}. Thus pure projection magnification fails as a weak-source path, with an explicit falsifier rather than a slogan.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit an MCSP-based route: set source object MCSP_{n,s} on N=2^n-bit truth tables, choose a concrete circuit model for the lower bound, state the exact threshold N^{1+epsilon} or smaller, and test whether the known magnification transfer is non-natural, target-preserving, and strong enough to imply SAT notin P/poly rather than only EXP or subexponential derandomization consequences.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is a valid conditional lemma, but the missing source object is an unconditional PRG/PRF with output length 2^m, output functions of size s, and security against 2^{Omega(m)}-size distinguishers. Proving that source object is itself a major lower-bound problem.
steps: Fix m, set N=2^m, and define MCSP_s on N-bit truth tables.
Assume for contradiction that a circuit C_N of size at most N^k decides MCSP_s.
Let D_N=1-C_N. This adds only O(1) gates, so D_N is within the promised security size.
By circuit counting, a uniformly random N-bit truth table is in MCSP_s with probability at most 2^{c s log s-N}. Thus D_N accepts uniform strings with probability at least 1-2^{c s log s-N}.
For every seed z, hardwire z into the bit-generator B_m(z,i). The resulting m-input circuit has size at most s, so G_m(z) is in MCSP_s and D_N rejects it.
Therefore D_N distinguishes uniform from G_m with advantage at least 1-2^{c s log s-N}, contradicting PRG security if the error bound is smaller.
Hence no such C_N exists. Since MCSP_s is in NP for s=poly(N), the target consequence is a conditional NP nonuniform lower bound, not an unconditional separation.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This does not prove P != NP. It relocates the burden to exponential-scale pseudorandomness and uses a naturalizing black-box interface; the transfer is route-level progress only.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: MCSP-PRF Transfer Audit

assumptions: Fan-in two circuit counting gives at most 2^{c s log s} m-input circuits of size at most s.
The MCSP threshold s satisfies s log s << N, e.g. s=m^d, so low-complexity truth tables are sparse.
For every seed z, G_m(z) is the truth table of a function computed by a circuit of size at most s.
The PRG/PRF security guarantee is nonuniform and covers size N^k+O(1) distinguishers.
MCSP_s is encoded so that witness circuits of size s can be verified in poly(N) time.
definitions: source object: a truth-table PRG/PRF family G_m:{0,1}^{r(m)} -> {0,1}^{N}, N=2^m, whose bit-generator B_m(z,i) has size q(m) and q(m)<=s(m).
target object: the nonuniform lower bound MCSP_s notin SIZE(N^k), where MCSP_s contains exactly the N-bit truth tables of m-input functions with circuit size at most s(m).
controlled interface: assume a small target circuit C_N for MCSP_s and use D_N=1-C_N as a black-box distinguisher between uniform N-bit strings and outputs of G_m.
target-preserving condition: the same size threshold s must certify all PRG outputs as yes-instances of MCSP_s, and PRG security must hold against circuits as large as the hypothetical MCSP circuit.
security scale: adversaries have size polynomial in N, equivalently exponential in m; ordinary poly(m)-security is insufficient.
barrier status: the argument is a valid natural-proof contraposition, not an escape from naturalization.

equations.label: counting_sparsity
equations.valid_when: Valid when N=2^m, circuits have fan-in two, s>=m, and c bounds the standard circuit-counting encoding.

equations.label: distinguisher_advantage
equations.valid_when: Applies when C_N exactly decides MCSP_s and every PRG output truth table has circuit size at most s.

equations.label: security_transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires nonuniform PRG security against N^k-size distinguishers and the same threshold s used by MCSP.

equations.label: np_transfer
equations.latex: MCSP_s\in NP\ \wedge\ MCSP_s\notin SIZE(N^k)\Rightarrow NP\not\subseteq SIZE(n^k)
equations.valid_when: Valid when s is polynomial in N and the lower bound holds on infinitely many input lengths.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if security is only against poly(m)-size distinguishers, if PRG outputs exceed the MCSP threshold, or if s log s approaches N, the transfer is invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Positive conditional bridge lemma plus barrier audit: it extracts an exact MCSP lower-bound consequence from an exponentially secure low-complexity PRG, while showing that the proof is naturalizing rather than a P vs NP proof.
candidate_lemmas.statement: PRF-to-MCSP transfer: let N=2^m and let MCSP_s be the language of N-bit truth tables of m-variate Boolean functions with circuit size at most s=s(m). If a length-N PRG/PRF G_m has every output truth table computable by circuits of size at most s, and fools nonuniform N^k-size distinguishers with error below 1-2^{c s log s-N}, then MCSP_s is not in SIZE(N^k). Since MCSP_s is in NP for s=poly(N), this conditionally gives NP not subset SIZE(n^k), but only from the source PRF assumption.

assumptions: The target lower bound is against polynomial-size circuits in the truth-table length N.
The PRF parameter is the number m of input variables for the represented Boolean function.
definitions: source object: ordinary small-parameter PRF security quantified over distinguishers of size m^{O(1)}.
target object: nonuniform MCSP lower bound against SIZE(N^k) on truth tables of length N=2^m.
controlled interface: the reduction turns a target circuit C_N into a distinguisher D_N of essentially the same N-scale size.
target-preserving condition: the source security parameter must dominate the target circuit size after substituting N=2^m.

equations.label: scale_conversion
equations.valid_when: Valid when the MCSP input is a full truth table of an m-variable Boolean function.

equations.label: insufficient_security
equations.valid_when: Valid in the asymptotic regime m to infinity with fixed target exponent k>0.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: any proposed source assumption stated only at poly(m) adversary size does not reach the target SIZE(N^k) lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Blocks an overclaim: standard polynomial-in-m pseudorandomness is too weak for this MCSP transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Security-scale mismatch lemma: a PRF secure only against m^{O(1)}-size algorithms cannot certify MCSP_s notin SIZE(N^k), because the distinguisher induced by a hypothetical MCSP circuit has size N^k=2^{km} in the PRF parameter m.

assumptions: Circuit descriptions of size s have O(s log s) bits.
The distinguisher accepts the complement of MCSP_s.
definitions: source object: sparsity of truth tables with m-variable circuit size at most s.
target object: largeness needed for the complement of MCSP_s to distinguish uniform strings from low-complexity PRG outputs.
controlled interface: the only quantitative parameter passed to the distinguisher is the density of high-complexity truth tables.
target-preserving condition: the chosen MCSP threshold must remain below the circuit-counting saturation point.

equations.label: largeness
equations.valid_when: Valid when the circuit-counting upper bound applies to all functions accepted by MCSP_s.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: a route using near-maximal s cannot claim the same natural distinguisher advantage.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Density-threshold lemma: the natural-property advantage used in L5.1 collapses unless c s log s is bounded away from N. For s=m^d the advantage is near one; for s near N/log N the counting estimate no longer supplies a strong distinguisher.

dependency_updates.description: Naturalization is converted into a contrapositive transfer: if MCSP_s had small circuits, its complement would be a large useful property and would break the source PRG/PRF.
The reduction is black-box in the hypothetical MCSP circuit and therefore does not supply a nonrelativizing feature for P vs NP.
No algebraic extension or low-degree representation is used; the argument remains outside algebrization claims but also gives no nonalgebrizing mechanism.
The source security must be against N^k-size distinguishers, equivalently 2^{km}-size distinguishers in the m-variable parameter.
The PRG output-size bound q(m)<=s(m) and target circuit-size bound N^k must be preserved without advice hidden in the encoding.

falsifier: after hardwiring the seed, the PRG output function has circuit size greater than the MCSP threshold s.
falsifier: s log s is too close to N, so the complement of MCSP_s is not large enough for the claimed advantage.
falsifier: the MCSP encoding includes advice or parameters not covered by the NP verifier and target SIZE(N^k) model.
falsifier: the route advertises an unconditional NP lower bound while relying on the source PRG/PRF hardness assumption.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 5 obtains a concrete quantitative transfer: exponentially secure low-complexity PRG/PRF outputs imply MCSP_s notin SIZE(N^k) with advantage threshold 1-2^{O(s log s)-N}. The useful bottleneck is not the slogan that MCSP is tied to natural proofs, but the exact adversary scale N^k and the threshold s log s << N. This is valid route-level progress and not evidence by itself for P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The remaining gap is source construction: no known MCSP reduction or meta-complexity argument produces a uniform constant-gap sequence of explicit no-side tables at threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
steps: Let f_i:{0,1}^{m_i}-> {0,1} be the function with truth table Y_i.
For each target length t choose i with m_i<=t<m_{i+1} and define L_t(u,v)=f_i(u), where |u|=m_i and v contains the padding bits.
Uniformity: compute i by enumerating the computable m_j up to t, then compute the requested bit of Y_i in time 2^{O(m_i)}<=2^{O(t)}; therefore L is in E.
Lower bound: if a circuit D of size S computes L_t, fixing all padding inputs to 0 gives a circuit of size S for f_i. Thus S>=C(Y_i)>2^{epsilon m_i}.
Since t<m_{i+1}<=kappa m_i+O(1), for every delta<epsilon/kappa and all large t one has 2^{epsilon m_i}>2^{delta t}.
Therefore the bridge lemma is valid: a dense uniform no-side MCSP carrier transfers to all-length E hardness with exponent delta<epsilon/kappa.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a conditional route lemma only. It does not construct the carrier, does not separate P from NP, and a downstream IW consequence would be BPP=P rather than P!=NP.

assumptions: Boolean circuit size C(.) is fan-in-2 nonuniform circuit size over the usual basis, and fixing input variables never increases size.
epsilon>0 and kappa are constants independent of i; delta is any fixed constant with delta<epsilon/kappa.
For all sufficiently large i, Y_i is a valid MCSP no-instance: C(Y_i)>2^{epsilon m_i}.
The interval index i(t) and the bit Y_i[x] are computable uniformly within 2^{O(t)} time.
definitions: source object: a uniform sequence (m_i,Y_i) where Y_i is a truth table in {0,1}^{2^{m_i}}, m_i is strictly increasing, bit access to Y_i[x] is computable in 2^{O(m_i)}, and Y_i is on the no-side of MCSP at threshold 2^{epsilon m_i}.
target object: a language L in E=DTIME(2^{O(n)}) whose length-t slice L_t has Boolean circuit complexity greater than 2^{delta t} for all sufficiently large t.
controlled interface: on input w of length t choose the unique i with m_i<=t<m_{i+1}, define L(w)=Y_i[prefix_{m_i}(w)], and ignore all padding bits.

target-preserving condition: the sequence m_i is uniformly computable, has multiplicative gap m_{i+1}<=kappa m_i+O(1), and the table-selection and bit-access procedures use no advice or nonuniform selector.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any source with unbounded m_{i+1}/m_i, epsilon_i tending to 0, or advice-based choice of Y_i; then the transfer gives at most sparse or nonuniform hardness.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Proves the target-preserving extraction theorem for the MCSP carrier interface under a dense uniform no-side source. It quantifies exactly how the threshold epsilon and carrier gap kappa transfer to the target exponent delta.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For constants epsilon>0 and kappa<infinity, a uniform constant-gap sequence of MCSP no-instances Y_i of variable lengths m_i with C(Y_i)>2^{epsilon m_i} yields an L in E such that C(L_t)>2^{delta t} for every sufficiently large t and every delta<epsilon/kappa. This is a route-level bridge to E hardness and IW-style derandomization, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: The transfer must preserve lower bounds only through restrictions or projections from L_t to Y_i.
No additional independent hard table is supplied for intermediate target lengths.
definitions: source model: high-MCSP tables Y_i with C(Y_i)>2^{epsilon m_i}.
target model: all-length E hardness C(L_t)>2^{delta t}.
interface limitation: L_t is obtained from Y_i by adding dummy or padding variables and then possibly applying uniform relabeling.

candidate_lemmas.statement: For padding transfers that reuse a hard m_i-bit slice to cover lengths t in [m_i,m_{i+1}), the best guaranteed all-length exponent at the upper endpoint is at most epsilon*m_i/(m_{i+1}-1). Hence superconstant carrier gaps collapse the constant-exponent target needed by IW.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier is now required to be a uniform constant-gap no-side sequence (m_i,Y_i), not merely MCSP hardness or isolated high-complexity truth tables.
Padding-density transfer proves L in E with all-length C(L_t)>2^{delta t} for every delta<epsilon/kappa.
Full-table existence is insufficient; bit access, interval computation, and carrier selection must be uniform and advice-free.

The padding extraction itself relativizes and cannot separate P from NP. A natural-proofs issue arises only if the carrier construction is a polynomial-time large useful property; nonuniform leakage remains the immediate barrier for this route.
